title: Evaluation and adjoint factorizations from local projective quotients
statement: Let $g:Z\to X$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $(V_j)_{j\in J}$ be an open covering of $X$, set $Z_j=g^{-1}(V_j)$ and $g_j=g|_{Z_j}$, and suppose that for every $j$ there are a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{V_j}$-module $E_j$ [pqf-def-coherent], an immersion $i_j:Z_j\to\mathbf P_{V_j}(E_j)$ over $V_j$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and a chosen isomorphism $i_j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong N|_{Z_j}$. Projective bundles, twists and their tautological quotients are as in [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry, def-per-projective-bundle-quotient-data], and pullback is tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Write $q_j:g_j^*E_j\twoheadrightarrow N|_{Z_j}$ for the pulled tautological quotient using the chosen isomorphism. Define $F=g_*N$ by $F(V)=N(g^{-1}V)$ and let $\varepsilon:g^*F\to N$ be the counit of module pullback/direct-image adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. Then $g$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], $F$ is quasi-coherent, and $\varepsilon$ is surjective. Under the sectionwise identification $(g_j)_*(N|_{Z_j})=F|_{V_j}$, the adjoint $\alpha_j:E_j\to F|_{V_j}$ of $q_j$ satisfies $q_j=\varepsilon|_{Z_j}\circ g_j^*\alpha_j$. There is a unique classifying morphism $r:Z\to\mathbf P_X(F)$ over $X$ for the quotient $(N,\varepsilon)$, with a quotient-compatible isomorphism $r^*\mathcal O(1)\cong N$. No finite-type or local-freeness assumption on $E_j$ is imposed.

proof.text: For each $j$, the projection $p_j:\mathbf P_{V_j}(E_j)\to V_j$ is separated by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], which allows arbitrary quasi-coherent $E_j$. Since $i_j$ is an immersion, [lem-trf-immersion-over-separated-base] gives separatedness of $g_j=p_j\circ i_j$. Applying the separatedness clause of [lem-sfb-separated-lfp-target-open-locality] to the given open cover $(V_j)$ proves that $g$ is separated. The cover need not be finite and $X$ need not be quasi-compact.

By [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated], $g$ is quasi-separated. By [def-sc-invertible-module], $N$ is quasi-coherent. Quasi-compactness of $g$ is a hypothesis of the item, so the two morphism hypotheses of [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] now hold; that theorem gives quasi-coherence of $F=g_*N$. Its direct image is the sectionwise module direct image of [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. No coherence or finite-type conclusion is used.

proof.text: Write $t_j:p_j^*E_j\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O(1)$ for the tautological quotient of [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. Pullback preserves epimorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-epi-direct-sum]. Using the composition isomorphism of [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition] to identify $i_j^*p_j^*E_j$ with $g_j^*E_j$, and the chosen isomorphism $i_j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong N|_{Z_j}$, the pullback $i_j^*t_j$ is the surjective quotient $q_j$ in the statement.

source.place: Tag 01VR, lemma-relatively-very-ample, proof (2) implies (4), before the immersion comparison

proof.text: For every open $W\subseteq V_j$, both $((g_j)_*(N|_{Z_j}))(W)$ and $(F|_{V_j})(W)$ equal $N(g^{-1}W)$, with the same restrictions and scalar action. This gives the claimed sectionwise identification. Apply [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] to $g_j$ and $q_j$ to obtain its unique adjoint $\alpha_j:E_j\to F|_{V_j}$. For any adjunction $L\dashv R$, the inverse adjunction bijection sends $a:A\to RB$ to $\varepsilon_B\circ L(a)$; this is the defining counit formula (or follows from naturality and the triangle identity). Consequently $q_j=\varepsilon^{(j)}\circ g_j^*\alpha_j$, where $\varepsilon^{(j)}$ is the counit for $g_j$. Open pullback is restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction]; its composition comparison is [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition]. Under these identifications $\varepsilon^{(j)}=\varepsilon|_{Z_j}$: both maps send a tensor germ $a\otimes s$ to $a s$ in $N_z$, where $s$ is represented by a section of $N$ over $g^{-1}W$, $W\subseteq V_j$. This proves the specified factorization with the actual counit.

source.place: Tag 01VR, lemma-relatively-very-ample, proof (2) implies (4), before the immersion comparison

proof.text: Fix $z\in Z$ and choose $j$ with $g(z)\in V_j$. Given a germ $n\in N_z$, the surjectivity of $q_j$ from Step 3 supplies a germ $e\in(g_j^*E_j)_z$ with $(q_j)_z(e)=n$. By Step 4, $n=\varepsilon_z((g_j^*\alpha_j)_z(e))$. Thus every stalk map $\varepsilon_z$ is surjective, which is precisely surjectivity of this module-sheaf map. Equivalently, local lifts along $q_j$ give local lifts along $\varepsilon$ on the covering $(Z_j)$.

source.place: Tag 01VR, lemma-relatively-very-ample, proof (2) implies (4), before the immersion comparison

proof.text: Apply the quotient classification in [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] with base $X$, quasi-coherent module $F$ (Step 2), $T=Z$, $h=g$, and the invertible quotient $(N,\varepsilon)$ (Step 5). The bijection gives an $X$-morphism $r:Z\to\mathbf P_X(F)$ and a quotient-compatible isomorphism $r^*\mathcal O(1)\cong N$. Injectivity of the same bijection makes $r$ unique among morphisms classifying this quotient. This uses neither finite type nor local freeness of $F$ or of any $E_j$.
